benchmark_title: Wave 1 Silicon Bake-Off Part A: AEAD Cipher & Hardware Instruction Proof

crate_kernel_findings.ring_0_17_14: Runtime CPUID dispatches to stitched 256-bit AVX2 VAES + VPCLMULQDQ kernel (ring_core_0_17_14__aes_gcm_enc_update_vaes_avx2 / dec_update_vaes_avx2) operating on ymm12..ymm15 + ymm1..ymm6 in both baseline and native builds (0.350 cpb L2).
crate_kernel_findings.aws_lc_rs_1_19_0: On x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, aws_lc_0_47_0_crypto_gcm_avx512_enabled compiles unconditionally to '33 C0 C3' (xor eax, eax; ret), dead-stripping aws_lc_0_47_0_aes_gcm_encrypt_avx512 from the final PE binary and falling back to 128-bit xmm VEX kernel aws_lc_0_47_0_aesni_gcm_encrypt (_aesni_ctr32_ghash_6x) at 0.656 cpb L2.
crate_kernel_findings.aes_gcm_0_10_3: In baseline-x86_64, cpufeatures dispatches to SSE/AES-NI (16 xmm0..xmm15 registers), spilling AES-256 round keys onto [rsp+40h..60h] with legacy 2-operand aesenc + pclmulqdq (2.169 cpb L2). With -C target-cpu=native, LLVM unlocks EVEX xmm16..xmm31 (zero round-key stack spills), 3-operand vaesenc, vpclmulqdq, and AVX-512 vpternlogq (1.353 cpb L2, +60.6% L2 / +107.1% 8T streaming).
